text:
Two stories follow Filip Hronek right now: the trade talk and the ice time. Daily Hive reported an insider saying teams have already tried to trade for him, NHLTradeRumor.com floated Dallas, and Boston Hockey Now included him in a Bruins roundup. Meanwhile Jeff Paterson of Rink Wide posted that "no one in the #NHL is playing more than #Canucks Filip Hronek this month."

The minutes are real: 26.7 a night on the season and 28.3 over his last ten, with three games above 30. The production is quiet: 15 points (one goal) in 24 games with nine on the power play, close to the pace that got him 49 points last season.

What worries us is five-on-five. With Hronek on the ice, Vancouver has taken only 36% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and chances against pile up when he plays. Evolving-Hockey valued him at 1.6 wins last season, mostly from the power play, and notes his teammates rank in the bottom 6%, which drags his raw numbers down. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis argued they "need to stop playing Filip Hronek so much." Whether the workload eases, or he moves, is what to watch.
